content.value_statement: Teams need a clear system overview before discussing lower-level architecture. This skill produces C4 context documentation with personas, journeys, dependencies, and Mermaid diagrams.
actual_capabilities: Creates high-level system descriptions for a C4 System Context view.
Documents personas, goals, features, and user journeys.
Identifies external systems and dependencies with integration purpose.
Produces Mermaid C4Context diagrams using standard C4 notation.
Links context documentation to container and component documentation.
Keeps architecture output readable for non-technical stakeholders.
limitations: It does not inspect source code automatically.
It requires accurate system, user, and dependency inputs.
It focuses on context-level views, not container or component internals.
It references a playbook file that is not included in this package.

use_cases.title: Plan stakeholder architecture reviews
use_cases.description: Create a shared system overview before deeper technical discussions.

use_cases.title: Document product-facing user journeys
use_cases.description: Map personas, goals, features, and journey steps for a product system.

use_cases.title: Prepare onboarding architecture notes
use_cases.description: Summarize system boundaries, external systems, and key interactions for new engineers.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic context view
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new system overview.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create C4 Context documentation for [system]. Include a short description, main users, external systems, and a Mermaid context diagram.

prompt_templates.title: Map personas and journeys
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for user-centered architecture documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a C4 Context document for [system]. Identify personas, key features, user goals, and journey steps for each major feature.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize existing architecture notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the provided container, component, and product notes to create a C4 Context document for [system]. Highlight boundaries and dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Review and refine context model
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this C4 Context documentation for clarity, missing personas, missing external systems, and stakeholder readability. Suggest concrete improvements.

output_examples.input: Create context documentation for a customer billing portal.
output_examples.output: A stakeholder-facing document with a system description, billing personas, payment journeys, external payment services, and a Mermaid context diagram.

output_examples.input: Identify external systems for a support ticket platform.
output: Identity provider for authentication and user roles.
Email service for notifications and inbound ticket creation.
Customer database for account and entitlement data.

output_examples.input: Review a draft C4 Context document for executive readability.
output_examples.output: A concise review that flags missing personas, unclear system boundaries, excess implementation detail, and weak dependency descriptions.

best_practices: Start with business goals, primary users, and the system boundary.
Keep diagrams focused on people, software systems, and external dependencies.
Link context documentation to deeper container and component views.
anti_patterns: Do not include deployment details in a context-level diagram.
Do not omit programmatic users or external service consumers.
Do not create diagrams before confirming system scope and audience.

faq.question: What C4 level does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports the C4 System Context level, which is the highest-level C4 architecture view.

faq.question: Can it create Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for Mermaid C4Context diagrams with people, systems, and relationships.

faq.question: Does it replace container or component documentation?
faq.answer: No. It complements those views by creating a higher-level stakeholder summary.

faq.question: What inputs improve the output?
faq.answer: Useful inputs include system purpose, target users, external systems, key features, and existing architecture notes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for non-technical stakeholders?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions emphasize stakeholder-friendly wording and avoiding low-level implementation details.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
